substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Investigation: Europe and the Mediterranean world (c. 600–1750 CE)

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Medieval Europe

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the features of castles and churches of the period, such as Warwick Castle in England and Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris, as examples of the Church’s power in terms of its control of wealth, land and labour

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the nature of illuminated manuscripts and recognising that the medieval manuscripts of monastic scribes contributed to the survival of many ancient Greek, Roman and Arab literary texts

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the changing relations between Islam and Europe, including the consequences of the Crusades and trade

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the impact of the Magna Carta on social groups, including the nobility, religious orders, merchants, workers/craftsmen, peasants and women

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the consequences of the Black Death on human populations using studies of church records from the period, considering the reliability of these statistics and explaining the impact of the population change in areas such as farming, commerce, culture and religion

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E07 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The Ottoman Empire

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E08 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the way of life of people in the Ottoman Empire, for example the role of the coffee house and bazaar or marketplace

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E09 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a selection of primary sources to track changes to the way of life in the Ottoman Empire across time and/or locations

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E10 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the power and responsibility of the Sultan to ensure that justice was served within society

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E11 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the importance of Islam in the Ottoman Empire

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E12 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Vikings

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E13 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating Viking lands in Scandinavia (Denmark, Norway and Sweden)

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E14 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the way of life of the Vikings, for example living in a cold and harsh environment, the importance of farming and raids, the significance of honour in Viking warrior society

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E15 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the social structures of Viking societies

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E16 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the system of Viking religious beliefs and their impact on the organisation of society

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E17 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Renaissance Italy

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E18 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the significance of double-entry bookkeeping, as seen in the Messari accounts of the Republic of Genoa in 1340 CE, in accelerating the production of wealth and patronage

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E19 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating learning in the Renaissance period (e.g. humanism and the influence of ancient Greece and Rome) and analysing the symbolic representation of this learning in architecture, artworks and inventions from individuals such as Brunelleschi, Copernicus, Donatello, da Vinci, Michelangelo and Titian

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E20 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining why the Catasto of 1427 CE was introduced in Florence following the end of war with the Duchy of Milan

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E21 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying a range of primary sources, such as artwork, music, literature, architecture, correspondence and diaries, that demonstrate the spread of the Renaissance across Europe

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E22 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The Spanish and the Americas

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E23 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing pre-Columbian life in the Americas, including the social organisation of the Aztecs (e.g. nobility, slaves), their beliefs (e.g. worship of a number of gods and the need to make human sacrifices to appease these gods) and life in the capital city, Tenochtitlan

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E24 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The emergence of the modern world in Europe

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E25 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the impact of the printing press on the rise of literacy

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E26 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the Enlightenment ideas about human freedom and the exercise of authority, which promoted radical change to the political order, for example constitutional government and the separation of Church and state

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E27 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining how rulers in different European nations responded differently to new and dissenting ideas that were emerging by comparing the responses of France, England, Spain and Russia

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K19-E28 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the way of life in key features of the French Ancien Régime and how it represented increasing centralisation of administrative power in the monarchy

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH8K20 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: causes and consequences of a significant event, development or turning point that contributed to continuity and change
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Investigation: Europe and the Mediterranean world (c. 600–1750 CE)

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Medieval Europe

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the causes and consequences of significant developments, such as the migrations of Germanic, Hun and Slavic peoples into western and central Europe, the rule of Charlemagne, the Norman invasion of England, the first Crusade and the impact of plague

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the impacts of the Church in the development of western European political and social institutions, such as kingship

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the causes of the formation of the feudal order and its impacts on European societies

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The Ottoman Empire

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing Ottoman art and architecture, such as Selimiye Mosque in the city of Edirne in Türkiye, and Islamic geometric design

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E07 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the role of warfare in expanding Ottoman territory, including the sieges of Bursa (1317–1326 CE) and Nicaea (1328–1331 CE)

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E08 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: outlining inventions and developments in the Islamic world, such as the astrolabe, public hospitals and libraries, and their subsequent adoption in the Western world

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E09 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the impact of the Crusades in challenging the Ottoman Empire and the responses of the Ottomans to the challenge

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E10 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Vikings

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E11 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the role of gods such as Odin, Thor, Frey and Freyja in Viking religion and the consequences of the adoption of Christianity on Viking culture

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E12 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the significance of the construction of longboats and their role in exploration, including innovations in keel and sail design, as factors contributing to change in Viking society

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E13 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and analysing evidence of Viking trade between Russia (Kiev) and the east (through Constantinople)

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E14 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing Viking craft with particular emphasis on the production of weapons and armour (e.g. swords, battle axes and helmets) and the effectiveness of these in battle

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E15 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the triggers of declining Viking power, such as the Battle of Stamford Bridge, the treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte, new colonies, changing climate and/or the spread of Christianity

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E16 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Renaissance Italy

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E17 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the Black Death and the fall of Constantinople as a trigger of the Renaissance

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E18 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a concept map or visual display to organise notes about the significant developments and/or cultural achievements that reflect the concentration of wealth and power in the city-states, such as art, learning and the invention of the printing press

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E19 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the artwork of Leonardo da Vinci, such as the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, and his inventions, including a rudimentary helicopter and solar power

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E20 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating learning in the Renaissance period, for example humanism, astrology, alchemy, the influence of ancient Greece and Rome

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E21 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the achievements of Galileo, such as his improvements on the telescope and his astronomical observations

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E22 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The Spanish and the Americas

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E23 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the arrival of Spanish conquistadors in Mexico and Peru from 1510 CE (Balboa) to 1531 CE (Pizarro), and their reasons, such as seeking wealth, claiming land for their king, converting the local populations to Christianity and a sense of adventure

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E24 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the significance of Alexander VI’s papal decrees of 1493 CE as a factor legitimising Spanish territorial expansion and claims in the Americas

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E25 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: outlining the consequences of Columbian exchange, such as the spread of disease; the introduction of crops, such as maize, beans, tobacco, chocolate and potatoes, to Europe; the encomienda system; mining and deforestation; and the impact of the loss of natural resources

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E26 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the longer-term consequences of conquest and colonisation on the indigenous populations of the Americas, such as the unequal distribution of land and wealth, slavery, political inequality, and imposition of Spanish culture and language over conquered territories

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E27 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The emergence of the modern world in Europe

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E28 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: considering the causes and consequences of a key development of the period, such as movable type and the translation of the Bible into vernacular languages

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K20-E29 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the consequences of the Reformation and/or the Enlightenment on the political organisation of Europe

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH8K21 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: experiences and perspectives of rulers and ruled, and the interaction between power and/or authority
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Investigation: Europe and the Mediterranean world (c. 600–1750 CE)

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Medieval Europe

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the impact of the Black Death on daily life using primary sources such as Matteo Villani’s diary, Boccaccio’s Decameron, Fordun’s Chronicle of the Scottish Nation and Ibn Khaldun’s recollection of the impact of the plague

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the reasons for different punishments for different groups of people, such as trial by combat as a privilege granted to the nobility and ducking stools as a punishment for women, and the use of punishment as a deterrent

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing how rulers responded to demands from the lower classes to improve their working conditions and lives following the plague, using sources such as King Edward III’s Statute of Labourers

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The Ottoman Empire

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: outlining the millet system that regarded non-Muslim people as subjects but as not being subject to Islamic law

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E07 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the importance of eunuchs, such as Beshir Agha in the 18th century, in the palace structure

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E08 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the tolerance of the Ottomans towards Christians and Jews

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E09 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Vikings

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E10 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the attacks on monasteries such as Lindisfarne (793 CE) and Iona (795 CE) and reviewing the written accounts of monks that contributed to the Vikings’ reputation for pillaging and violence

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E11 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the survival of a heroic Iron Age society in early medieval Ireland, as described in the vernacular epics, and its transformation by the spread of Christianity, the influence of the Vikings and the Anglo-Norman conquest

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E12 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the remains of Viking settlements, such as Dublin (Ireland) and Jorvik (York)

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E13 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Renaissance Italy

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E14 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the differing levels of political involvement in city-states, such as the guilds in Florence and Libro d’Oro in Venice

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E15 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing primary sources to understand the interactions between the rulers of Florence, Venice, Naples and/or the Papal States

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E16 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The Spanish and the Americas

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E17 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing encounters between Hernán Cortés and the Aztecs, and the siege of Tenochtitlan (1521 CE)

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E18 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the impact of the Spanish on the indigenous populations of the Americas (e.g. the introduction of new diseases, horses and gunpowder, and the loss of natural resources)

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E19 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The emergence of the modern world in Europe

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E20 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the changes in the role and the power of monarchies in the political systems of western Europe, for example the decline of absolutism, development of parliaments and new ideas relating to nationalism

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K21-E21 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the continuities and changes in the political power of the bourgeoise and peasant classes with the growth of cities and increased urbanisation, and the movement of peoples

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH8K22 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: the role and contribution of a significant individual and/or group to change
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Investigation: Europe and the Mediterranean world (c. 600–1750 CE)

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Medieval Europe

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the role of the Catholic Church in medieval Europe in providing social services, such as education, health care and social welfare, and in feudal village organisation

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the influences and contributions of individuals such as Gregory the Great, Charlemagne, Alfred the Great and Hildegard of Bingen

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The Ottoman Empire

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the contributions of the Janissaries to the Ottoman Empire, including as the first modern standing army in Europe and the Mediterranean world

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing historians’ interpretations of the achievements of individuals such as Selim I in establishing the empire and capturing Jerusalem, or Suleiman the Magnificent in expanding the empire into Europe

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E07 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Vikings

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E08 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: outlining Erik the Red’s development of Viking settlements in Eastern and Western Greenland in 985 CE

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E09 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the artefacts discovered at L’Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland (Canada) with Viking artefacts as possible evidence that the Vikings had journeyed to North America 500 years before Christopher Columbus

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E10 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Renaissance Italy

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E11 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the influence of the Medici family in Florence as bankers and merchants, and their patronage of the arts

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E12 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the influences and contributions of individuals such as Lucrezia Borgia, Galileo, Lorenzo de Medici, Leonardo da Vinci and Niccolo Machiavelli

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E13 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The Spanish and the Americas

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E14 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the significance of key chronological events in the lives of individuals, such as Columbus, Balboa, Cortés, Montezuma II and/or Pizarro

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E15 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The emergence of the modern world in Europe

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E16 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the role and achievements of Henry VIII, Elizabeth I and Martin Luther

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E17 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the importance of the Scientific Revolution, in particular the scientific theories and discoveries of Copernicus, Galileo, Kepler and Newton, for overturning traditional views of the motion of the planets, and how these contributed to science being seen by many as an alternative to the Church as a source of fundamental truth about reality

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K22-E18 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the role and significance of Oliver Cromwell and the execution of Charles I in the English Civil War in the development of the Westminster parliamentary system

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Medieval Europe

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining how historians have disproved medieval myths such as King Arthur or Pope Joan

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the impact of the Black Death on Europe with reference to differing historians’ interpretations

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The Ottoman Empire

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the contrasting perspectives on the Fall of Constantinople (1453 CE), including prophecies and legends, and how these shaped historians’ interpretations of the experience of people living at the time

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Vikings

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E07 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the extent to which historians’ interpretations are corroborated with the oral histories contained in Icelandic sagas, such as about Erik the Red founding Greenland

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E08 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: reviewing representations of Vikings in modern films, games and popular culture

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E09 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Renaissance Italy

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E10 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the importance of key women in Renaissance society, such as Caterina Sforza (1463–1509 CE), Isabella d’Este (1474–1539 CE), Lucrezia Borgia (1480–1519 CE) and Catherine de Medici (1519–1589 CE), using a range of artwork, written sources and historians’ interpretations to justify claims

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E11 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The Spanish and the Americas

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E12 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the extent to which historians’ interpretations that the Spanish conquest can be attributed to the pursuit of ‘Gold, God and Glory’ differ

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E13 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The emergence of the modern world in Europe

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E14 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining how the interpretations of the discoveries of science are linked to ideas about the free exercise of human reason and how that could lead to improvements and progress in human life and society generally

elaborations.name: VC2HH8K23-E15 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining historical interpretations of key events, developments or achievements during this period, such as the Scientific Revolution or the beginnings of the Age of Reason/Enlightenment, and how these interpretations highlight their importance or significance to contemporary society

elaborations.name: VC2HH8S01-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing a key question, such as ‘How were the pyramids at Giza built?’, and understanding that there may not be a definitive answer; identifying related questions to inform the inquiry, including ‘What evidence is there?’ and ‘What theories have been developed?’

elaborations.name: VC2HH8S01-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing questions using historical concepts, such as cause, consequence, continuity, change, perspectives, interpretations and significance, for example ‘What were the consequences of rising sea levels on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples during Deep Time?’

elaborations.name: VC2HH8S01-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing a key question, such as ‘How did Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People respond to changing climatic and environmental conditions?’ or ‘How did the decline of Rome’s western empire change the organisation of European society?’, and subsidiary questions, such as ‘What evidence is there?’ and ‘What interpretations are there?’ to inform the inquiry

elaborations.name: VC2HH8S01-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing questions about historical significance, such as ‘How were communities affected by the Black Death?’ and ‘How long did it last?’

elaborations.name: VC2HH8S01-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: reviewing questions when faced with unexpected or challenging developments posed by the historical investigation, for example ‘How was the organisation of Japanese society influenced by world events?’

elaborations.elaboration_text: defining terms, such as ‘Deep Time’, ‘Everywhen’, ‘Pleistocene’, ‘Holocene’, ‘BC (Before Christ)’, ‘AD (Anno Domini)’, ‘BCE (Before Common Era)’, ‘CE (Common Era)’, ‘Before Present (BP)’, ‘pre-history’ and ‘history’

organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 9 and 10, students study the history of the modern world.

During this period, a globalised world took shape, as societies connected through ideas, trade, migration, technological advancements, colonisation, war and peace to bring us to the present day. Students learn about the 2 world wars of the 20th century, their causes and connections, and the consequences that still influence society today, with a particular focus on Australia. They investigate Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ movements that have promoted rights and freedoms in the modern era. Students can enhance these investigations by re-examining colonial Australia and/or by exploring how Australia has developed since World War II to become the country it is today. Students also learn about at least one Asian society from 1750 to the present, including its relationship with European powers, contributions in the world wars and movements of independence over the 20th century.

Students are required to study at least 5 Historical Knowledge and Understanding sub-strands (the Overview sub-strand and at least 4 Investigation sub-strands). They can choose whether to study one or both of the Investigation: Australia (1750–1914) and Investigation: The globalising world (1945–present) sub-strands. Within some Investigation sub-strands students have a choice of topics (found within the elaborations). See the summary in the table below.

Historical Knowledge and Understanding sub-strandTopics
Overview: Levels 9 and 10–
Investigation: Australia (1750–1914)*–
Investigation: Australians at war (1914–1945)–
Investigation: Asia (1750–present)

Choose at least one of:

  • China
  • India
  • Indonesia
  • Japan
  • Vietnam
Investigation: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ rights and freedoms (1938–present)–
Investigation: The globalising world (1945–present)*

Choose at least one of:

  • Popular culture
  • Environment movement
  • Migration experiences
  • Political crisis
  • Regional and global conflict

* Students can choose whether to study one of or both the Australia (1750–1914) and The globalising world (1945–present) investigation sub-strands.

In this band, students build on their understanding and application of the interrelated historical concepts and skills to the historical knowledge of national histories, including Australia’s, and the impacts of global developments in the modern era by asking and modifying historical questions; sequencing chronology; evaluating historical evidence, perspectives and interpretations; analysing continuity and change, and causes and consequences; evaluating historical significance; and presenting their historical interpretations with terms, knowledge, conventions and evaluated evidence from a range of historical sources.

Historical questions provide a focus for students’ historical investigations. The following are examples only and may be used or adapted to suit local contexts:

  • What shapes the modern world?
  • How have global developments shaped Australia?
  • What are the causes and consequences of war?
  • How do individuals contribute to change?

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 10, students evaluate the significant events, developments and ideas that shaped the modern world, including histories of Australia, the world wars and the Holocaust, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ rights and freedoms over the period between 1750 and the early 21st century.

Students formulate and adapt historical questions to support the development of historical investigations and their use of historical sources and concepts to interpret the modern world. They organise historical narratives of events, ideas and developments in chronological order to explain varied patterns and forms of continuity and change and their causes and consequences. Students analyse the key features of primary and secondary sources, their content and context, and apply historical questions when drawing inferences from them. They evaluate historical sources by verifying and corroborating their accuracy and value as historical evidence. Students use historical sources to identify and analyse the perspectives of individuals and groups in the modern world and use these perspectives to understand the beliefs, values and attitudes of the individuals and societies studied. Students recognise the contested nature of history and apply this knowledge to identify and evaluate different historical interpretations and debates. Students analyse varied patterns and forms of continuity and change and analyse the significant events, individuals, ideas and development that contributed to and resulted from them. They analyse short- and long-term causes and intended and unintended consequences of significant events, individuals, ideas and developments and their relationships to continuity and change. They use criteria informed by historical questions to evaluate the historical significance events, ideas, individuals, groups, movements and developments of the modern world. When constructing sustained historical interpretations, students use historical concepts, terms, relevant knowledge, conventions and evaluated evidence from a range of historical sources.

elaborations.elaboration_text: examining how convicts transported to Australia were able to begin new lives away from the rigid class structures of English society, with many of them making significant contributions to the emerging colonial society, such as Francis Greenway and Samuel Terry

content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K13 - History
content_descriptions.text: the causes of World War I and World War II

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K13-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a concept map to analyse the causes of World War I or World War II

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K13-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and describing the long-term causes of World War I, such as militarism, the alliance system among European countries in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, imperialism and nationalism, and short-term triggers of World War I, such as the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary, the ‘July Crisis’ and the invasion of Belgium by Germany

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K13-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying significant events and ideas between World War I and World War II, including the Treaty of Versailles, the Russian Revolution, the Great Depression and the rise of Adolf Hitler and the Nazi Party in Germany from 1933, and evaluating their significance as causes of World War II

content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K31 - History
content_descriptions.text: the significant events, developments, campaigns and movements for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ rights and freedoms
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Investigation: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples' rights and freedoms (1938–present)

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K31-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a timeline of significant events and developments that contributed to or influenced campaigns for rights and freedoms between 1938 and the present, with events and developments including the Pilbara strike, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the Commonwealth Electoral Act (1962), the Freedom Rides, the 1966 Wave Hill Walk-Off, the 1967 Referendum, the establishment of the Aboriginal Embassy in Canberra, the 1988 bicentenary protest, the Mabo decision (Mabo v Queensland (No 2) 1992) the Native Title Act (1993), the Bringing Them Home report and National Sorry Day (the Stolen Generations), the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, Closing the Gap, the Apology, the Uluru Statement from the Heart and the 2023 Voice Referendum

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures- VC2CCPACP2
organising_ideas.text: The occupation and colonisation of the land now known as Australia by the British, under the now overturned doctrine of terra nullius, were experienced by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples as an invasion that denied their occupancy of, and connection to, Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples are the Traditional Owners of Country and Place, protected in Australian law by the Native Title Act 1993, which recognises pre-existing sovereignty, continuing systems of law and customs, and connection to Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people belong to the world’s oldest continuous cultures. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples demonstrate resilience in the maintenance, practice and revitalisation of culture despite the many historic and enduring impacts of colonisation, and they continue to celebrate and share the past, present and future manifestations of their cultures.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures- VC2CCPACP2
organising_ideas.text: The occupation and colonisation of the land now known as Australia by the British, under the now overturned doctrine of terra nullius, were experienced by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples as an invasion that denied their occupancy of, and connection to, Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples are the Traditional Owners of Country and Place, protected in Australian law by the Native Title Act 1993, which recognises pre-existing sovereignty, continuing systems of law and customs, and connection to Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people belong to the world’s oldest continuous cultures. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples demonstrate resilience in the maintenance, practice and revitalisation of culture despite the many historic and enduring impacts of colonisation, and they continue to celebrate and share the past, present and future manifestations of their cultures.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.

content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K30 - History
content_descriptions.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ experiences and perspectives of colonisation and resistance between 1788 and 1938
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Investigation: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples' rights and freedoms (1938–present)

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K30-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the diverse experiences of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples during the period, including individuals and groups who maintained connection with Country and Place, lived on missions and reserves, in urban settings and in community

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures- VC2CCPACP2
organising_ideas.text: The occupation and colonisation of the land now known as Australia by the British, under the now overturned doctrine of terra nullius, were experienced by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples as an invasion that denied their occupancy of, and connection to, Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples are the Traditional Owners of Country and Place, protected in Australian law by the Native Title Act 1993, which recognises pre-existing sovereignty, continuing systems of law and customs, and connection to Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people belong to the world’s oldest continuous cultures. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples demonstrate resilience in the maintenance, practice and revitalisation of culture despite the many historic and enduring impacts of colonisation, and they continue to celebrate and share the past, present and future manifestations of their cultures.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.

content_descriptions.sub_strand: Investigation: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples' rights and freedoms (1938–present)

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K32-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the lives of significant Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and other Australians who contributed to their rights and freedoms, such as Neville Bonner, William Cooper, Fred Maynard, Jack Patten, Douglas Nicholls, Gladys Nicholls, Vincent Lingiari, Charles Perkins, Shirley Smith, Gladys Elphick, Essie Coffee, Joyce Clague, Daisy Bindi, Gary Foley, Michael Anderson, Eddie Koiki Mabo and Lowitja O’Donoghue

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures- VC2CCPACP2
organising_ideas.text: The occupation and colonisation of the land now known as Australia by the British, under the now overturned doctrine of terra nullius, were experienced by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples as an invasion that denied their occupancy of, and connection to, Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples are the Traditional Owners of Country and Place, protected in Australian law by the Native Title Act 1993, which recognises pre-existing sovereignty, continuing systems of law and customs, and connection to Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people belong to the world’s oldest continuous cultures. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples demonstrate resilience in the maintenance, practice and revitalisation of culture despite the many historic and enduring impacts of colonisation, and they continue to celebrate and share the past, present and future manifestations of their cultures.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K32-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander groups that contributed to changing Australian society, such as the Australian Aborigines League (Victoria), the Australian Aboriginal Progressive Association (AAPA), Student Action for Aborigines, the First Peoples’ Assembly of Victoria and other groups within Australian states working towards treaties

content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K36 - History
content_descriptions.text: changing historical perspectives over time in relation to the developments in technology, public health, longevity and standards of living in the 20th century, and concern for the environment and sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K36-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating and comparing advertisements for technology since 1945

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K36-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing sources to track changes in public health and standards of living since 1945, such as sources from the United Nations Development Programme or in the online publication Our World in Data

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K36-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining how attitudes to the environment and sustainability have developed in Australia, including a change in focus from conservation to addressing climate change

content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K40 - History
content_descriptions.text: the historical perspectives of those who experienced a major global influence, development and/or event, and how these perspectives may have changed over time, including Australian and global perspectives

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Popular culture

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting generational perspectives on popular music

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing a selection of relatives about their experiences in their teens, tracking the changing perspectives through the 20th and 21st centuries and suggesting reasons for these changes

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The environment movement

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining why environmental movements gained increasing public and political voice and identifying different perspectives, such as a shift from conservation and anti-nuclear movements to responding to climate change

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Migration experiences

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E07 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using sources to analyse the changing attitudes to the arrival of migrants over time

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E08 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the arguments for and against the White Australia Policy between 1964 and 1973

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E09 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing members of their community about their experiences of migrating to Australia and presenting an evaluation of their perspectives based on wider research

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E10 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Political crisis

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E11 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing a selection of different historical sources from Australia about a political crisis or conflict

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E12 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting a range of different perspectives on the extent of continuity and change in relation to a political crisis or conflict

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E13 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Regional and global conflict

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E14 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using historical sources to analyse different perspectives of people experiencing the conflict and how these perspectives may have changed over time and why these perspectives have changed

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E15 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating sources from the international community on the conflict, such as the United Nations or Human Rights Watch

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E16 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining why a range of perspectives still exists in relation to the conflict

content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10S05 - History
content_descriptions.text: analyse the perspectives, beliefs, values and attitudes of people and groups based on evidence from a range of sources

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S05-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing whether the perspective of one individual in the period is representative of a majority or minority view at that time

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S05-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and explaining the different beliefs, values and attitudes of people and groups in the past as expressed in sources, such as diaries, oral accounts, letters, laws, propaganda and popular culture

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S05-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining why some perspectives, beliefs, values or attitudes in the past may not have been recorded

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S05-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining different accounts of 18th-century journeys to Australia, such as ships’ logs, diaries and recorded testimonies of male and female convicts, and officers, and explaining the variations in perspective that can lead to different historical interpretations

as_extracts.name: HHIS10-E07
as_extracts.description: Students recognise the contested nature of history and apply this knowledge to identify and evaluate different historical interpretations and debates.

content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K12 - History
content_descriptions.text: interpretations and debates about Australian history between 1750 and 1914, including the Frontier Wars or Australia as social laboratory

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K12-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the interpretation of the colonisation of Australia as an invasion

organising_ideas.text: The occupation and colonisation of the land now known as Australia by the British, under the now overturned doctrine of terra nullius, were experienced by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples as an invasion that denied their occupancy of, and connection to, Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples are the Traditional Owners of Country and Place, protected in Australian law by the Native Title Act 1993, which recognises pre-existing sovereignty, continuing systems of law and customs, and connection to Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people belong to the world’s oldest continuous cultures. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples demonstrate resilience in the maintenance, practice and revitalisation of culture despite the many historic and enduring impacts of colonisation, and they continue to celebrate and share the past, present and future manifestations of their cultures.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures- VC2CCPACP2
organising_ideas.text: The occupation and colonisation of the land now known as Australia by the British, under the now overturned doctrine of terra nullius, were experienced by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples as an invasion that denied their occupancy of, and connection to, Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples are the Traditional Owners of Country and Place, protected in Australian law by the Native Title Act 1993, which recognises pre-existing sovereignty, continuing systems of law and customs, and connection to Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people belong to the world’s oldest continuous cultures. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples demonstrate resilience in the maintenance, practice and revitalisation of culture despite the many historic and enduring impacts of colonisation, and they continue to celebrate and share the past, present and future manifestations of their cultures.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures- VC2CCPACP2
organising_ideas.text: The occupation and colonisation of the land now known as Australia by the British, under the now overturned doctrine of terra nullius, were experienced by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples as an invasion that denied their occupancy of, and connection to, Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP3

organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.

content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10S07 - History
content_descriptions.text: analyse continuity and change

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S07-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying different manifestations or consequences of an event, such as World War I or World War II, in different geographical locations

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S07-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using sources of evidence (perspectives and interpretations) to identify continuity and changes during Australia at the turn of the 20th century

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S07-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using chronologies to observe and identify patterns where changes or continuities have occurred in Australian history between 1750 and 1914

as_extracts.name: HHIS10-E09
as_extracts.description: They analyse short- and long-term causes and intended and unintended consequences of significant events, individuals, ideas and developments and their relationships to continuity and change.

content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K01 - History
content_descriptions.text: causes and consequences of the Industrial Revolution, the movement of people and European imperialism

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K01-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the significant technical developments of the Industrial Revolution and their impacts on manufacturing, social organisation and trade

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K01-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and describing the causes of the movement of peoples in the modern world, including the push factors (e.g. the Agricultural Revolution, the Industrial Revolution, the Irish Potato Famine, discrimination and persecution, and forced migration, such as slavery and convict settlements) and pull factors (e.g. the promise of a better life, employment opportunities, space and personal freedom)

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K01-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and describing the consequences of imperialism on colonised peoples, such as dispossession, disease and destruction of existing social structures and cultures

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K01-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining data on the movement of peoples in the period, such as the number of slaves transported and the nations/places involved, including Portugal, Britain, France, Spain and North America, or the number of people forced to migrate from Ireland because of the potato famine, and the nations/places they emigrated to, such as the USA, Canada and Australia

content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K03 - History
content_descriptions.text: significant developments and events since 1945 that have contributed to global change, such as World War II, the United Nations, the Cold War and technologies

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K03-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key developments in technology since 1945 that have changed the world in the following areas: the household, such as television, appliances, central heating and cooling; travel and trade, such as shipping and passenger jets; globalisation, mass consumption and communications, such as the microchip, satellites and digital systems

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K03-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating an annotated timeline of major global social, economic, political, technological and cultural developments between 1945 and the present, including events such as the end of World War II, the establishment of the United Nations, the Cold War, key conflicts of the Cold War, decolonisation, development of the transistor, manned space flight, the end of the Cold War, development of personal computers and information technology, the War on Terror, the Global Financial Crisis, the COVID-19 pandemic and the emergence of new global economic powers

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K03-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the growth in the world’s population during the 20th century, including life expectancy changes in different parts of the world, and the depletion of natural resources

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K03-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying how the rise of the environmental movement around the world has changed people’s perspectives on things such as developments in renewable energy technology and sustainability measures, such as recycling

content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K21 - History
content_descriptions.text: significant events, individuals and developments of the Holocaust

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K21-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the key phases of the Holocaust, including identification, exclusion, ghettoisation, deportation, mass murder and liberation

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K21-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the roles of organisations and individuals associated with the Holocaust, such as the Nazi Party, the SS, Adolf Hitler, the civilian population, the collaborators in occupied countries and complicit governments

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K21-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the significance of events and developments associated with the Holocaust, such as the Nuremberg Laws or the Wannsee Conference

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K21-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: mapping and comparing how occupied countries responded to the Nazi genocidal programs in eastern and western Europe

content_descriptions.text: the causes and consequences of contact with other countries and/or colonisation and liberation of a society

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K09-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the key steps to Federation, such as the Australasian Federation Conference (1890), the first Federal Constitutional Convention (1891), the second Federal Constitutional Convention (1897–1898), the first referendum on the Federal Constitution (1898), the second referendum on the Federal Constitution (1899), the Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act (1900) and Federation Day (1 January 1901), and evaluating the contribution of key groups and individuals, such as Sir Henry Parkes, Sir Samuel Griffith, William Guthrie Spence, John Feltham Archibald, Catherine Helen Spence, Alfred Deakin, Tom Roberts, Frederick McCubbin, Arthur Streeton, Joseph Furphy, Barbara Baynton, Banjo Paterson, Henry Lawson, ‘Federation leagues’, the Australian Natives Association and The Bulletin

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K09-E06 - History

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K10-E05 - History

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K11 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: continuities and changes and their consequences on ways of life, living conditions, political and legal institutions and cultural expression around the turn of the 20th century

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K11-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the living and working conditions in Australia around 1900 and making comparisons between different settings using sources such as photographs, paintings, diaries and newspapers

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K11-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the social and political impact of religious sectarianism between Protestants and Catholics in the formation of the Australian nation

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K11-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the main features of housing, sanitation, transport, education, agriculture and industry that influenced living and working conditions in Australia around 1900 and comparing them with early colonisation around 1800

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K11-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining how laws made by the federal parliament, such as those resulting from the Harvester Judgement or the introduction of pensions, affected working conditions and standards of living

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K12 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: interpretations and debates about Australian history between 1750 and 1914, including the Frontier Wars or Australia as social laboratory

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K12-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the interpretation of the colonisation of Australia as an invasion

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures- VC2CCPACP2
organising_ideas.text: The occupation and colonisation of the land now known as Australia by the British, under the now overturned doctrine of terra nullius, were experienced by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples as an invasion that denied their occupancy of, and connection to, Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples are the Traditional Owners of Country and Place, protected in Australian law by the Native Title Act 1993, which recognises pre-existing sovereignty, continuing systems of law and customs, and connection to Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people belong to the world’s oldest continuous cultures. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples demonstrate resilience in the maintenance, practice and revitalisation of culture despite the many historic and enduring impacts of colonisation, and they continue to celebrate and share the past, present and future manifestations of their cultures.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K13 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: the causes of World War I and World War II

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K13-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a concept map to analyse the causes of World War I or World War II

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K13-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and describing the long-term causes of World War I, such as militarism, the alliance system among European countries in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, imperialism and nationalism, and short-term triggers of World War I, such as the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary, the ‘July Crisis’ and the invasion of Belgium by Germany

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K13-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying significant events and ideas between World War I and World War II, including the Treaty of Versailles, the Russian Revolution, the Great Depression and the rise of Adolf Hitler and the Nazi Party in Germany from 1933, and evaluating their significance as causes of World War II

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K13-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the major events leading up to the outbreak of World War II, such as the Japanese invasion of Manchuria, the Spanish Civil War, the Italo-Abyssinian Wars, the annexation of Austria, the Munich Agreement and the annexation of the Sudetenland, the invasion of Poland in 1939, the occupation of China and the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941
