elaborations.name: VC2HH10K13-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the impacts of the Treaty of Versailles on Germany, the structural weaknesses of the League of Nations, the rise of fascist and militarist regimes, and the failure of appeasement policies as factors contributing to World War II

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K14 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: the reasons that Australians, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, fought in the world wars

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K14-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the different perspectives towards war at the beginning of the 20th century, such as notions of war as noble and heroic or as an adventure, and the significance of loyalty to Britain as an aspect of Australian identity

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K14-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the responses of Australia’s political leaders to the outbreak of war, such as prime minister Andrew Fisher’s pledge to back Britain ‘to the last man and the last shilling’

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K14-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the reasons why Australian men enlisted in the Australian Imperial Force, for example the challenges of living on the land and a need for a regular pay; adventure; to do their duty for the British Empire; the impact of persuasive propaganda posters, pamphlets and leaflets; peer and community pressure

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K14-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the stories of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander men who enlisted in the Australian Imperial Force

organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K14-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the reasons for Australia’s involvement in World War II and prime minister Robert Menzies’ ‘Australia is also at war’ speech

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K14-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting the reasons for Australia’s involvement in World War I and World War II

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K15 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: significant places where Australians fought

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K15-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the places where Australians fought during World War I, such as Gallipoli, Fromelles, the Somme, Pozières, Passchendaele, Bullecourt, Villers-Bretonneux, the Sinai Peninsula, Gaza and Beersheba

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K15-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying places where Australians fought during World War II, such as Greece, North Africa (including Tobruk), Darwin, New Guinea (including Kokoda), Malaya and Singapore, and evaluating their significance to Australia’s war effort and to the war as a global conflict

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K16-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting the different experiences of combat between 1914 and 1945, noting distinctions between the experience of infantry on the Western Front and the Light Horse in Palestine during World War I and that of soldiers in the Greek campaigns, North Africa and the Pacific theatres, naval personnel and aircrews of World War II

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K16-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching the roles of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander service personnel during World War I and World War II

elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the experiences of Australian women deployed overseas during World War I and World War II, such as nurses, using historical sources

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K16-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the perspectives of those who fought or were deployed overseas using sources such as diaries, letters and newspapers

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K16-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the experiences of various prisoners of war (POWs), such as the treatment of Australian POWs under German and Japanese control

elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the perspectives of particular groups of prisoners of war (POWs), such as those in camps in Ambon or Rabaul, those used as forced labour on the Thai-Burma Railway, or army nurses captured in Singapore

substrand_content_descriptions.text: significant events and turning points of the world wars

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K17-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the significance to Australia of one major World War I battle or campaign, such as Gallipoli, Fromelles, the Somme, Pozières, Passchendaele, Bullecourt, Villers-Bretonneux or Beersheba, and then evaluating its significance to the war from a global perspective

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K17-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining why particular events in Europe between 1939 and 1945, such as Germany’s invasion of Poland in 1939, Operation Barbarossa, Stalingrad, the D Day landings and the Soviets’ capture of Berlin, are significant

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K17-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: ranking the significance of key events and developments of the Asia-Pacific conflict between 1941 and 1945, such as the bombing of Pearl Harbor, the fall of Singapore, the Kokoda campaign, the bombing of Darwin, the Battle of Midway, Iwo Jima, and the dropping of the atomic bombs on Japan

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K18-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the targeting of civilian populations in World War I and World War II and explaining the significance of these differences

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K18-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the nature of trench warfare and the development of military technology, such as the use of tanks, aeroplanes and chemical weapons (gas), during World War I

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K18-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating changing aspects of warfare during World War II, such as Blitzkrieg, air power, bombing campaigns, mass mobilisation of society, targeting of civilian populations and atomic weapons

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K18-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the race to build the atomic bomb and analysing why the atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki

elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the consequences of the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, including short- and long-term consequences on human health and short- and long-term environmental impacts on the cities and surrounding areas

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU1
organising_ideas.text: The nations of Asia influence historical and contemporary global relationships, including international responses to global developments and events.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K19 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: significant consequences of the world wars on Australian society and the experiences and historical perspectives of those on the home front, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and women

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K19-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the consequences of World War II on the changing roles of women in Australia during the war, for example women in the military, the Women’s Land Army and factory work, contrasted with the continuities of their roles before and after the war

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K19-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the impact of World War II at a local and national level, such as the bombing of Darwin, the Japanese submarine attack on Sydney and the sinking of ships off the Australian coast, the ‘Battle of Brisbane’, the Cowra breakout and the Brisbane Line

organising_ideas.text: The nations of Asia influence historical and contemporary global relationships, including international responses to global developments and events.

organising_ideas.text: Australia and Asia are interdependent through a range of historical and contemporary connections.

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K19-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the consequences of changes to individual rights and freedoms because of the National Security Act 1939, such as censorship of the media; detention of Japanese, German and Italian residents; banning groups opposed to the war on political or religious grounds; and controls over the workforce (‘manpower controls’)

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K19-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the barriers that affected Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ enlistment in World War II, such as the lack of trust in their loyalty by the Australian Government, denial of their status as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Peoples and the notion that they would contribute to disharmony in the armed forces

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K19-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the reasons for the Australian Government changing its views on including Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Peoples in the defence forces, such as the critical shortage of soldiers, the Torres Strait Light Infantry Battalion established in 1941 and specialised work undertaken by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people, for example the Nackeroos and the Northern Territory Special Reconnaissance Unit

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K19-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the changing roles of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people working as civilians for the army during World War II, such as increased employment opportunities in domestic work in hospitals, ammunition stacking, timber cutting and cement works, maintaining gardens, slaughtering cattle, and assembling and clearing gearboxes

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K20 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: the causes of the Holocaust

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K20-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the meaning of racism, discrimination, antisemitism and genocide

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K20-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the global context and attitudes towards racism, anti-Semitism and genocide before and during World War II

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K20-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the historical context in which the Holocaust occurred, including Nazi ideology, Nazi propaganda, erosion of democracy and rise of fascism, racism and antisemitism, Nazi rule and racial policy in Germany before 1939

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K20-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the significance of ideology in Nazi racial and genocidal programs

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K21 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: significant events, individuals and developments of the Holocaust

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K21-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the key phases of the Holocaust, including identification, exclusion, ghettoisation, deportation, mass murder and liberation

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K21-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the roles of organisations and individuals associated with the Holocaust, such as the Nazi Party, the SS, Adolf Hitler, the civilian population, the collaborators in occupied countries and complicit governments

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K21-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the significance of events and developments associated with the Holocaust, such as the Nuremberg Laws or the Wannsee Conference

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K21-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: mapping and comparing how occupied countries responded to the Nazi genocidal programs in eastern and western Europe

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K22 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: the diverse experiences and perspectives of Jewish and non-Jewish peoples during the period of the Holocaust

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K22-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a biographical exhibition of the diverse experiences and perspectives of individual Jewish people during the Holocaust, with examples from a variety of countries, ages and experiences, such as emigrations, hiding, ghettoisation, work/death camps, conversions and joining the resistance

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K22-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the Nazi party’s racial policies as they related to other groups in Europe and Germany, such as people with disabilities, members of LGBQTI+ communities, and Sinti, Roma, Black and Slavic peoples, Soviet Communists and political prisoners

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K22-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining stories and accounts of Jewish resistance during the Holocaust, such as armed resistance, camp-based resistance, spiritual resistance and concealment

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K22-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the experiences and perspectives of non-Jewish people who protected or saved Jewish people during the Holocaust

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K23 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: different interpretations and debates about the significance and legacies of the world wars

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K23-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the impacts of war on returned soldiers, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander soldiers, such as physical and psychological trauma, shell shock, employment opportunities, social and racial discrimination, service recognition, land allocation (Soldier Settlement Scheme), wage inequality, and access to health care and pensions

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3

organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K23-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the ideals associated with the Anzac tradition and how and why World War I is commemorated within Australian society and discussing the similarities and differences in historians’ views of the Anzac legend over time

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K23-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the significance of World War I and/or World War II to Australia’s international relationships, such as with Britain, the USA, Asian countries and the United Nations

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K23-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating different historians’ interpretations of the significant short- and long-term legacies of World War II, such as the establishment of the United Nations, the occupation and reconstructions of Germany and Japan and international war crimes trials, as causes of the Cold War and decolonisation

organising_ideas.text: The nations of Asia influence historical and contemporary global relationships, including international responses to global developments and events.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K23-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the short- and long-term impacts of the Holocaust on the Jewish community after World War II, such as coming to terms with the scale of loss, migration to Israel, Australia and the USA, and the creation of Yad Vashem and other Holocaust centres, museums and memorials

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K23-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: debating the significance of the United Nations’ Universal Declaration of Human Rights as a legacy of World War II and the Holocaust

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K30 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ experiences and perspectives of colonisation and resistance between 1788 and 1938
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Investigation: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples' rights and freedoms (1938–present)

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K30-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the diverse experiences of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples during the period, including individuals and groups who maintained connection with Country and Place, lived on missions and reserves, in urban settings and in community

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures- VC2CCPACP2
organising_ideas.text: The occupation and colonisation of the land now known as Australia by the British, under the now overturned doctrine of terra nullius, were experienced by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples as an invasion that denied their occupancy of, and connection to, Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples are the Traditional Owners of Country and Place, protected in Australian law by the Native Title Act 1993, which recognises pre-existing sovereignty, continuing systems of law and customs, and connection to Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K31 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: the significant events, developments, campaigns and movements for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ rights and freedoms
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Investigation: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples' rights and freedoms (1938–present)

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K31-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a timeline of significant events and developments that contributed to or influenced campaigns for rights and freedoms between 1938 and the present, with events and developments including the Pilbara strike, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the Commonwealth Electoral Act (1962), the Freedom Rides, the 1966 Wave Hill Walk-Off, the 1967 Referendum, the establishment of the Aboriginal Embassy in Canberra, the 1988 bicentenary protest, the Mabo decision (Mabo v Queensland (No 2) 1992) the Native Title Act (1993), the Bringing Them Home report and National Sorry Day (the Stolen Generations), the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, Closing the Gap, the Apology, the Uluru Statement from the Heart and the 2023 Voice Referendum

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K36 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: changing historical perspectives over time in relation to the developments in technology, public health, longevity and standards of living in the 20th century, and concern for the environment and sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K36-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating and comparing advertisements for technology since 1945

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K36-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing sources to track changes in public health and standards of living since 1945, such as sources from the United Nations Development Programme or in the online publication Our World in Data

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K36-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining how attitudes to the environment and sustainability have developed in Australia, including a change in focus from conservation to addressing climate change

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K37 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: the origins and significance of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, including Australia’s involvement in the development of the declaration

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K37-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the causes of the development of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, such as the atrocities of the Holocaust and the immense scale of destruction and displacement because of World War II

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K37-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the present significance of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K37-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining how human rights have developed in Australia, including movements related to human rights and the introduction of human rights legislation such as the Victorian Charter of Human Rights

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K38 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: causes and consequences of significant post-1945 world events, ideas and developments, and their influences on Australia after 1945

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Popular culture

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining popular culture in Australia after World War II, including music, film and sport

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the influence music, film and sport has had on movements and vice versa

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing how music, film and sport have expressed, challenged and developed an Australian identity after World War II

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the role of technology and consumerism on popular culture

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The environment movement

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E07 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: outlining the origins of environmental movements in the campaigns to preserve the natural environment for future generations, for example the establishment of the USA’s Yellowstone National Park in 1872, Australia’s Royal National Park in 1879, Canada’s Rocky Mountains National Park in 1885 and New Zealand’s Tongariro National Park in 1887

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E08 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the impact of early texts that warned about environmental change, such as Silent Spring by Rachel Carson (1962), ‘Don’t It Make You Want To Go Home’ by Joe South (1970), Mother Earth News magazine (1970) and ‘Mercy Mercy Me (The Ecology)’ by Marvin Gaye (1971)

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E09 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the consequences of nuclear warfare and Mutually Assured Destruction in raising concerns about the environment

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E10 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining reasons why the United Kingdom conducted 12 major nuclear weapons tests in Australia between 1952 and 1957 at the Montebello Islands, Emu Field and Maralinga, and why opposition to the testing grew in the 1950s

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E11 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Migration experiences

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E12 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the causes and conditions that led to increased migration to Australia and changes to public opinion and government policy

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E13 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the main features of a government policy that affected migration to Australia, such as the Immigration Restriction Act 1901 and use of the dictation test to restrict the immigration of non-Europeans, and the ‘populate or perish’ government policy immediately following World War II

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASG1
organising_ideas.text: Australia’s deep and continuing relationships with the peoples of Asia develop and influence mutual understandings and expressions of citizenship and culture nationally, regionally and globally.

organising_ideas.text: Australia and Asia are interdependent through a range of historical and contemporary connections.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E14 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the nature of the waves of migration (e.g. from Europe in the 1950s–1960s, from different parts of Asia in the 1970s–2000s, from the Middle East in the 1980s–1990s, from India in the 1990s–2000s or from Africa in the 2000s), the numbers of migrants from those countries since World War II and the reasons for those migrations, including push factors such as the effects of war, economic downturns or social upheaval, and pull factors such as Australia’s peaceful democracy and economic and educational opportunities

elaborations.elaboration_text: Political crisis

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E16 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the causes and consequences of the Petrov Affair, including the influence of McCarthyism

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E17 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the developments during the Whitlam government and the causes of the government’s dismissal, including changing political ideologies

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E18 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the causes and the consequences of a conflict in which Australia participated, such as the Korean War, the Vietnam War, the Gulf War, Australian peacekeeping in East Timor, the War in Afghanistan or the Iraq War

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E19 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the changing of prime ministers while in government and the attitudes and effects of these changes, including Hawke to Keating (1991), Rudd to Gillard to Rudd (2010–2013) and Abbott to Turnbull to Morrison (2015–2018)

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E20 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Regional and global conflict

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E21 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the causes and the consequences of one regional or global conflict, such as the Cold War, the Korean War, the Vietnam War, Middle East conflicts, South Africa Apartheid, the Irish Troubles, the Balkans War, the War in Afghanistan or the Iraq War

organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K38-E22 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating how one regional or global conflict may or may not have influenced Australia, such as changing migration patterns, contribution of aid from Australia, how Australian society may have responded to regional or global events and how the communist victory in the Vietnam War resulted in the arrival of refugees into Australia and contributed to the abolishment of the ‘White Australia Policy’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K39 - History

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E01 - History

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the changing nature of the music, film and television industries in Australia during the post-war period, including the influence of overseas developments such as rock ‘n’ roll, disco, punk, hip hop, electronic dance music and other music genres; Hollywood, Bollywood, Korea and the animation film industry in China, Japan and Korea; and the development of satellite broadcast and streaming on television

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating Australia’s contribution to international popular culture in music, film, television and sport, and the recognition of Australian creative and performing arts internationally

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E04 - History

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining events such as the struggle over American, British and French nuclear weapon testing in the Pacific from 1946 to 1996 or the sinking of the Rainbow Warrior in 1985

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the effectiveness of international protocols and treaties such as Kyoto (1997), the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (since 1992, especially 2015) and the Washington Declaration (2007)

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E07 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the significance of the Franklin Dam protests in the 1970s and 1980s and their impact on Australian politics and law, including the establishment of a World Heritage Site, the Hawke government’s response and the subsequent Tasmanian Dams Case (The Commonwealth of Australia v Tasmania (1983))

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E08 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Migration experiences

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E09 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing how the communist victory in the Vietnam War resulted in the arrival of refugees into Australia and contributed to the abolishment of the ‘White Australia Policy’

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASG1
organising_ideas.text: Australia’s deep and continuing relationships with the peoples of Asia develop and influence mutual understandings and expressions of citizenship and culture nationally, regionally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASG2
organising_ideas.text: Australia and Asia are interdependent through a range of historical and contemporary connections.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E10 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating policies of multiculturalism, cultural diversity and inclusion since the 1970s and the concepts of cultural heritage and assimilation

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E11 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing post-World War II population growth and the development of Australia’s culturally diverse society using different types of graphs

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E12 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Political crisis

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E13 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and evaluating the continuities and changes to Australian society that resulted from a political crisis

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E14 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a chart or graphic organiser to categorise the continuities and changes associated with a political crisis

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E15 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Regional and global conflict

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E16 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and evaluating changes caused by one regional or global conflict, such as the dissolution of the USSR at the end of the Cold War or the end of Apartheid in South Africa

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K39-E17 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing continuities caused by the regional or global conflict, including social, political, economic, cultural, environmental and historical continuities

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10K40 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: the historical perspectives of those who experienced a major global influence, development and/or event, and how these perspectives may have changed over time, including Australian and global perspectives

elaborations.elaboration_text: Popular culture

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting generational perspectives on popular music

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing a selection of relatives about their experiences in their teens, tracking the changing perspectives through the 20th and 21st centuries and suggesting reasons for these changes

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The environment movement

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining why environmental movements gained increasing public and political voice and identifying different perspectives, such as a shift from conservation and anti-nuclear movements to responding to climate change

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Migration experiences

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E07 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using sources to analyse the changing attitudes to the arrival of migrants over time

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E08 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the arguments for and against the White Australia Policy between 1964 and 1973

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E09 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing members of their community about their experiences of migrating to Australia and presenting an evaluation of their perspectives based on wider research

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E10 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Political crisis

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E11 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing a selection of different historical sources from Australia about a political crisis or conflict

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E12 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting a range of different perspectives on the extent of continuity and change in relation to a political crisis or conflict

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E13 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Regional and global conflict

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E14 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using historical sources to analyse different perspectives of people experiencing the conflict and how these perspectives may have changed over time and why these perspectives have changed

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E15 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating sources from the international community on the conflict, such as the United Nations or Human Rights Watch

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K40-E16 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining why a range of perspectives still exists in relation to the conflict

elaborations.elaboration_text: Popular culture

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K41-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating contrasting historical interpretations of continuity and change in Australian popular culture since 1945

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K41-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: The environment movement

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K41-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the different interpretations of the significance of the environmental movement on political developments in Australia since 1975

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K41-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Migration experiences

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K41-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the debates about migration over time and the degree to which they have changed over time

elaborations.elaboration_text: Political crisis

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K41-E08 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the legacies of a political crisis, including different interpretations of these legacies

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K41-E09 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the legacies of a conflict, including on Australian society

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K41-E10 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating historical interpretations and debates on the degree to which a conflict has been effectively resolved

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K41-E11 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: Regional and global conflict

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K41-E12 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining a debate concerning the legacy of the conflict, including whether it is resolved

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K41-E13 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining interpretations from Australians on the conflict and its impact on Australia

elaborations.name: VC2HH10K41-E14 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the reasons for different interpretations concerning the intended and unintended consequences and changes a conflict created

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10S01 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: formulate, refine and use historical questions to inform historical investigations

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S01-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: changing a key question or related questions in an inquiry, depending on the suitability of the sources available

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S01-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing an inquiry question, such as ‘What were the causes of World War I?’, and refining it as further factors are introduced into the research process

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S01-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: modifying questions using historical concepts such as cause, consequence, continuity and change

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S01-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: modifying an inquiry question in response to suitability of evidence from available sources

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S01-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: determining whether a key question or related questions are too broad or narrow given the requirements of the investigation

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10S02 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: sequence significant events, individuals, ideas, movements and developments chronologically to analyse continuity and change, and causes and consequences

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S02-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating to develop a timeline of significant global developments and movements for change between a moment in the past and the present to identify continuities and changes over the period

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S02-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a timeline that identifies the significant events or individuals across a particular period, observing and discussing patterns of causation and change, and/or identifying parts of the world that were involved in or affected by a significant event

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S02-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising a range of primary sources and/or perspectives in chronological order to support the development of a historical argument about continuities or changes

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10S03 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: analyse the purpose, features, content and context of historical sources

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S03-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with a broad range of historical sources, including written materials, such as diaries, letters, speeches, newspapers, legislation and government reports; oral records, including interviews, accounts and stories; and visual sources, such as cartoons, photographs, paintings, film and video

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S03-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with a broad range of historical interpretations, including textbooks, the writings of historians, documentaries, films and fiction

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S03-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: preparing a table to summarise the types of sources available for the study of modern history and identifying the strengths and limitations of different source types

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S03-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the events, ideas, individuals and symbols represented in a visual source, such as racial stereotypes, characterisations of political figures or the use of the Hakenkreuz as a symbol of Nazism, which has been appropriated from the Hindu swastika

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S03-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the contextual significance of a source, such as Frank Hurley’s World War I photos, and identifying the purpose of Hurley’s creation of composite photos

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S03-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the context of a source, such as the Bringing Them Home report (1997), and the significance of that context in understanding responses to the source (with varying perspectives)

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures- VC2CCPACP2
organising_ideas.text: The occupation and colonisation of the land now known as Australia by the British, under the now overturned doctrine of terra nullius, were experienced by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples as an invasion that denied their occupancy of, and connection to, Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples are the Traditional Owners of Country and Place, protected in Australian law by the Native Title Act 1993, which recognises pre-existing sovereignty, continuing systems of law and customs, and connection to Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people belong to the world’s oldest continuous cultures. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples demonstrate resilience in the maintenance, practice and revitalisation of culture despite the many historic and enduring impacts of colonisation, and they continue to celebrate and share the past, present and future manifestations of their cultures.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10S04 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: evaluate the value of sources for use as evidence to interpret historical significance, continuity and change, and causes and consequences

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S04-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying that the reliability and usefulness of a source depends on the questions asked of it, such as an account having a particular historical perspective and therefore being of use in revealing past prevailing attitudes

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S04-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: determining the extent to which the accuracy or purpose of a source affects its usefulness

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S04-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting the range of perspectives at the time of a historical event and identifying voices that may be absent from the sources, such as those of women, men, children, ethnic groups, Indigenous peoples or minority groups

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S04-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying information in a primary or secondary source that is relevant to the historical questions being asked

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S04-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing a range of historical sources and identifying similarities, differences and inconsistencies

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S04-E06 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing a range of historical sources to identify long- and short-term causes and/or intended and unintended consequences of events

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10S05 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: analyse the perspectives, beliefs, values and attitudes of people and groups based on evidence from a range of sources

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S05-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing whether the perspective of one individual in the period is representative of a majority or minority view at that time

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S05-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and explaining the different beliefs, values and attitudes of people and groups in the past as expressed in sources, such as diaries, oral accounts, letters, laws, propaganda and popular culture

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S05-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining why some perspectives, beliefs, values or attitudes in the past may not have been recorded

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S05-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining different accounts of 18th-century journeys to Australia, such as ships’ logs, diaries and recorded testimonies of male and female convicts, and officers, and explaining the variations in perspective that can lead to different historical interpretations

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10S06 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: evaluate historical interpretations and debates

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S06-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring debates about the historical period or topic studied, such as the relative importance of the causes of World War I or the long- and short-term causes of World War II

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S06-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating a museum exhibition, film, documentary or video game as a historical interpretation

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S06-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the similarities and differences in historians’ views about colonial society, such as the emergence of a distinct Australian identity, the influence of the White Australia debate on the push for Federation and the idea of Australia as a ‘working man’s paradise’

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S06-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying different interpretations of specific events, such as the debate about conscription in Australia during World War I

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S06-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing how historians have changed the way they interpret the event under investigation over time, such as a change in view with the discovery of more sources (e.g. as with frontier conflicts in Australia)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10S07 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: analyse continuity and change

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S07-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying different manifestations or consequences of an event, such as World War I or World War II, in different geographical locations

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S07-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using sources of evidence (perspectives and interpretations) to identify continuity and changes during Australia at the turn of the 20th century

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S07-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using chronologies to observe and identify patterns where changes or continuities have occurred in Australian history between 1750 and 1914

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10S08 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: analyse short- and long-term causes and the intended and unintended consequences of significant events, individuals, ideas and developments and their contributions to continuity and change

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S08-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using graphic organisers, such as concept maps, causal spider webs, fishbone diagrams or ripple effect charts, to analyse causes and consequences of historical continuity and change

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S08-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: differentiating between intended and unintended consequences

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S08-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising causes and consequences of a historical development, such as European colonisation of Australia, World War I and World War II, into a concept map

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10S09 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: evaluate the significance of individuals, groups, movements, events, developments and ideas

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S09-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying a significant event, person or idea and evaluating its significance using the criteria of importance, profundity, quantity, durability and relevance

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S09-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing an explanation using sources of evidence to support the analysis of a significant individual, event and/or cultural achievement, and using consistent referencing and historical terms and concepts

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S09-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the significance of the fall of Singapore (1942) in the changes in Australia’s military alliances and use of troops during World War II, using a range of sources, such as accounts of prisoners of war; commanders such as General Gordon Bennett; politicians such as Prime Minister John Curtin, and Japanese and British sources

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU1
organising_ideas.text: The nations of Asia influence historical and contemporary global relationships, including international responses to global developments and events.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2HH10S10 - History
substrand_content_descriptions.text: construct sustained historical interpretations and arguments using appropriate historical concepts, terms, knowledge, conventions and evaluated evidence from a range of historical sources

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S10-E01 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using relevant historical and conceptual terminology (e.g. imperialism, colonisation, settler society, invasion, Agricultural Revolution, Industrial Revolution, migration and immigration, urbanisation, conflict, genocide, nationalism, Cold War, human rights, popular culture, environmentalism, source, perspective, interpretation, contested, continuity, change, cause, consequence, significance) in historical interpretations

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S10-E02 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing a historical argument that identifies different possibilities in interpretation, synthesises ideas to build an argument and presents a particular point of view that incorporates and evaluates available evidence

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S10-E03 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing an extended text that evaluates a historical event, development or movement

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S10-E04 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting a historical argument, such as an essay, oral presentation, debate, interactive digital or non-digital display, online conference or forum, incorporating evidence

elaborations.name: VC2HH10S10-E05 - History
elaborations.elaboration_text: using appropriate citation and referencing conventions, including the preparation of bibliographies that distinguish between primary and secondary sources
